title: Admiring Oliver and playing second cornet
summary: Armstrong says it was a big thing to be sent for by Oliver, whom he admired; he had few solos and did not yet sing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Was it a different kind of excitement to play with this band coming up from New Orleans for you, for the inspiration? It was a big thing for me.
Yeah. Yes it was. Because I admired Jim so much. For him to send for me I thought there was something.
Now did you get, in this band, when you were playing second cornet to him, did you get to play solos all by yourself too? Oh, very subtle.

There were like one or two records, I think it was chimes, blues, or something like that. But I never wanted to do that in Oval Joe. Did you sing at all? No. That came later? Yeah. Because he knew I was singing, but the main thing was to kind of play with him. And I was singing in a little quartet and he knew all of that, you know.
